problem:
The center of the hyperbola $3{x}^{2}-4{y}^{2}-12x+16y=28$ is$\,\,($
{{field-1}}$,$
{{field-2}}
$).$
worked_solution:
The equation of a horizontal hyperbola centered at $(h,k)$ is given by

$$
\frac{(x-h)^{2}}{{a}^{2}}-\frac{(y-k)^{2}}{{b}^{2}}=1.
$$

To rewrite the equation of the hyperbola in the above form, we need to group $x$ and $y$ terms and complete the squares, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}3{x}^{2}-4{y}^{2}-12x+16y & =28 \\ 3{x}^{2}-12x-4{y}^{2}+16y & =28 \\ 3[{x}^{2}-4x]-4[{y}^{2}-4y] & =28 \\ 3[(x-2)^{2}-4]-4[(y-2)^{2}-4] & =28 \\ 3(x-2)^{2}-12-4(y-2)^{2}+16 & =28 \\ 3(x-2)^{2}-4(y-2)^{2} & =28+12-16 \\ 3(x-2)^{2}-4(y-2)^{2} & =24 \\ \frac{(x-2)^{2}}{8}-\frac{(y-2)^{2}}{6} & =1 \\ \frac{(x-2)^{2}}{(\sqrt{8})^{2}}-\frac{(y-2)^{2}}{(\sqrt{6})^{2}} & =1.\end{aligned}
$$

Hence, the center of the hyperbola is $(\,2,2\,).$
